items.title: Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2022
items.q: Dan and I have often played that piece with our dad called “La Fiesta de la Posada.”

ctx.x: I think you’re right. That’s what he said. And Dave said, “I’m done with this” and she said, “No you’re not.” And I’ll have to show you, like I’m telling you a story about your father that you don’t know I guess. And then he went up and got up there and they were put up in an A frame and up in the top attic were all the Christmas decorations so he went up there and finished it. It’s just very touching.

Dan and I have often played that piece with our dad called “La Fiesta de la Posada.” And it usually would happen in December, these performances. And God, Christmas has gotten so just pukingly commercialized. I was trying to think of a worse word than disgustingly and I came up with that one. I don’t know if it’s a real word. But you would get the real sense of Christmas and love when you do this piece, “La Fiesta de la Posada” ‘cause it has a chorus, which is usually like town folk that like singing you know.…

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Danny was on cymbals. He was ten years old.

ctx.x: Yeah, for the Canadian Broadcasting Company.

There was a tough piece in a screwy time signature that whoever was on bass with my group at the time couldn’t get into it. He said, “Why don’t you have Chris play it?” You remember? So Chris came out, sight-read it on electric bass, and cut it perfectly. Danny was on cymbals. He was ten years old. So even hanging out at rehearsals, here’s a record session where the kids did something constructive.

I remember one time when Gerry Mulligan was at our house. The kids came home from school. I guess – I don’t know whether you invited them or what, but anyway, they – Chris and Dan started playing with you and Gerry. I remember when Gerry was packing up to go home, he said, “Boy, have you got it made. You have an in-house rhythm section.”

items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: There’s a recording, just came out last week in England with four of our sons and the London Symphony Orchestra.

ctx.x: Maybe I can just wrap up and ask about your sons’ careers. They seem to be going well.

Oh yeah. There’s a recording, just came out last week in England with four of our sons and the London Symphony Orchestra. So we’ve got the test pressing upstairs. And I’m pleased with it. It was for my 80th birthday. When I was 70 they brought the four sons, when I was 75, the four sons, 80. They bring them from all over the world, because Darius is in South Africa, and Danny and Matthew are in California. Chris is a mile or so from here. And we have a big party in England on my birthday. So this recording has a…
Wanted to give credit where it’s due, huh?
